challenge_pass.obvious_path: Grep for 'TheRealSynth', replace any hits, add a generic readiness doc, and separately just report 'pnpm build fails' as a blocker without investigating why.
challenge_pass.optimized_path: Grep for 'TheRealSynth' and classify hits by live-config vs. historical-evidence (finding: none exist at all here), and actually run pnpm build/lint to see what breaks rather than assuming it works or reporting a bare failure.
challenge_pass.non_obvious_path: Root-cause the build failure by iterating: fix the first blocking error (Turbopack panic) with a minimal patch-version bump matching a value already validated by a sibling migration mission in this same cohort, re-run, discover and fix the next blocking error it was masking (missing turndown types), re-run again -- treating the build failure as a diagnosable defect chain rather than a single opaque blocker, while stopping at the point where further fixes (lint tooling, test runner) would require net-new scope decisions and would risk conflicting with already-open, in-flight PRs (#29, #22) doing related work.
challenge_pass.cheapest_reversible_test: A single read-only recursive grep for 'TheRealSynth' (zero hits, immediately falsifying the hardcoded-hazard hypothesis for this repository) followed by directly running pnpm build to observe the actual failure mode rather than guessing at it -- both zero/low write risk, both fully discriminating before any edit.
challenge_pass.alternate_access_surfaces: GitHub API (get_check_runs on the most recent merged PR) to confirm the Vercel GitHub App integration is installed, the same way it was confirmed for the sibling GLH-PROD-002 repository; list_pull_requests to discover PR #29 and PR #22 already in flight against this exact repository before making any edit, to avoid duplicating or conflicting with that work.
challenge_pass.existing_assets_or_open_source: Reused the exact next version (16.2.6) already validated working in the sibling PFORG-MIG-GLH-PROD-002 mission's repository rather than guessing at an arbitrary patch version. Reused the readiness-doc structure and historical-evidence-preservation precedent from PFORG-MIG-IDEABIN-001 and PFORG-MIG-GLH-PROD-002. Deliberately did not reinvent test-runner/lint setup that PR #29 is already building.
challenge_pass.human_in_loop_option: The actual GitHub organization transfer, Vercel dashboard re-linking, GitHub App re-authorization, production environment-variable configuration, and setting up a lint/test toolchain from scratch are all owner-executed or product-decision actions enumerated as follow-ups/owner actions, not automated here.
challenge_pass.recommendation: Adopted the non-obvious path: root-caused and fixed the two pre-existing build-breaking defects with minimal, reversible, evidence-backed dependency edits; confirmed zero hardcoded-ownership hazards; documented Vercel/GitHub-App binding assumptions and owner actions; explicitly declined to fix the lint/test-runner tooling gaps to avoid scope creep and conflict with already-open PRs, recording them as follow-ups instead.
assumptions_challenged: Rejected reporting 'pnpm build fails' as an unexplained blocker; iteratively root-caused it to two distinct, unrelated defects and fixed both with minimal changes, verifying the fix twice (including a clean .next rebuild).

Rejected fixing pnpm lint and the orphaned test file just to have every acceptance command pass; verified both are pre-existing tooling gaps outside owns_paths/mission intent and that fixing the test runner specifically would risk conflicting with the already-open PR #29, so left both as documented follow-ups instead.
Rejected treating weightliteracy.org/info@weightliteracy.org as transfer hazards; confirmed they are the production business domain, explicitly out of scope.
Rejected inventing a lease_id or otherwise misrepresenting control-plane state; recorded the true null-lease/READY state honestly.

route_comparison.route: obvious: report the build/lint failures as a blocker without investigating root cause, or blanket-fix everything found (lint config, test runner, build) in one pass
route_comparison.tradeoffs: Reporting as a bare blocker wastes the mission's own instruction to distinguish and fix safe issues; blanket-fixing everything (lint toolchain choice, test-runner choice) would introduce net-new tooling decisions and directly risk merge conflicts with the already-open, in-flight PR #29 which is independently adding a test runner.

route_comparison.route: non-obvious (chosen): root-cause and fix only the two build-breaking defects with minimal, evidence-backed, reversible dependency edits reusing a version already validated in a sibling migration mission; explicitly stop short of the lint/test-runner tooling gaps and record them as follow-ups
route_comparison.tradeoffs: Leaves two acceptance-adjacent items (lint, an orphaned test file) unresolved, but avoids inventing tooling choices outside this mission's authority/owns_paths and avoids duplicating or conflicting with PR #29's in-flight work -- the safer, more scope-disciplined outcome for a migration-readiness mission specifically.

challenge_pass.material_difference: The chosen route changes what evidence backs the mission's conclusion: instead of an unexplained 'build fails' status or an over-broad tooling rewrite, the deliverable is a diagnosed defect chain (Turbopack panic -> masked type-declaration gap) fixed with two minimal, version-matched, already-validated-elsewhere edits, plus an honest boundary drawn at the tooling gaps that require net-new scope decisions and would conflict with already-open work. This changes the actual risk surface (verified build health vs. an assumed blocker) and the workflow (reusing a sibling mission's validated fix vs. guessing at a fix, and deferring to an already-in-flight PR vs. duplicating it).
